chunks: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

Whoever is content with what suffices him from this world, the least of what is in it will be enough for him. And whoever is not content with what suffices him from this world, nothing in it will ever be enough for him.

key_terms.أَيْسَرُ الَّذِي فِيهَا: the least and easiest portion of what the world contains
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life and its material provisions
key_terms.بِمَا يُجْزِيهِ: with that which is enough and sufficient for him
key_terms.يَكْفِيهِ: will suffice him and meet his need

ai.seo_question: How does contentment with the world affect a person's sense of sufficiency?
ai.summary: This saying teaches qana'ah: contentment with a sufficient share of worldly life. It explains that true sufficiency is tied to inner satisfaction, while lack of contentment makes worldly possessions endlessly inadequate.
